# Native regression-driver first sources

Issue: [#223](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/issues/223). This bounded
session preserves the original test-driver inputs before opt-in consolidation.
It changes no production acceptance or mathematical meaning.

The [first record](first.json.gz) retains the fourteen-file static source
inventory, eleven original generated Lean bodies and the first mechanical
refactor diagnostics. Its SHA-256 is
`fc386407b882f08962f884b80a58f9780d4f136922b2ed5c808da6f5860c70cb`.
The compressed record is 226,264 bytes; its bounded expanded JSON is 1,177,131
bytes. The passive reader is `scripts/test_native_driver_bundle.py`.

The generated bodies were captured at local commit
`7af7634bcee3cf3e0d3b6203489e32a8013af036`, before any original Lean main was
compiled or executed. The eleven relevant Python modules, including the
harness, have identical original bytes at the consolidation base
`299e8f47bf9fb1973dd6ad2aba46fdee6a610f97`. The older static inventory retains
its own original revision and scope; it is not a new validation result.

The first extraction script refused before writing because it selected three
different output files in the exact comparator. The next extraction changed
indentation inside QFT's Lean string literal. Exact comparison retained that
counterexample and stopped after nine earlier source matches. The repair
preserves literal bytes; all eleven original generated bodies then matched.
Neither refusal came from native acceptance or a quantum execution.

The [first combined compilation](first-compilation.json.gz) preserves six
actual source/report records. The pinned Lean compiler rejected `IO.getArgs`
in the new dispatcher; static-library preparation completed, but no original
driver or quantum case ran. The repair passes command-line arguments through
the ordinary `main (args : List String)` entrypoint. The archive is 109,849
bytes (1,009,115 bounded expanded bytes), SHA-256
`9eacf796ce40c5f0da8a65ea4fa8f56b3aa8ccb558a7bd6e4ac39a86416f62a1`.
It does not supply a successful native test or proof.

The [first comparison](first-comparison.json.gz) retains 16 actual records:
the interference comparison matched, then QFT's native process completed but
its Python report refused because the extracted generator did not return
`upper`. Shared QFT and selector-refusal probes were not reached. Returning
the original bound repairs reporting without changing generated Lean bytes.
This archive is 39,564 bytes (130,820 bounded expanded bytes), SHA-256
`db9c44eb1b0daf93b5a7a6e249dd053c126a98a0f20b28a5f5bdf04055b934d1`.
Its partial observation is not complete shadow or performance evidence.

The [first policy refusals](first-policy.json.gz) retain eight actual records,
including the nineteen-command expectation, VM-22/29 preimages and explicit
technical review of all four changed frozen comparators. Their complete Python
ASTs are unchanged apart from selector keywords and the argv adapter. Refreshing
these reviewed identities does not change boundaries, capacities or proof
coverage. The new harness/selection helpers are additionally frozen as untrusted
regression source. The archive is 181,364 bytes (822,843 bounded expanded bytes),
SHA-256 `332568ca403e2b7c91a37282afb6259f555618ac5f02f8a1b5eb4ad0eea5110b`.

Five drivers consume generic JSON, while six generated bodies embed the
existing cases (including distinct literal/small-semantic QFT commands).
All original assertions, oracles, seeds, timeouts and bounds remain separate
from this passive source record. Historical Rust-authority report labels stay
inside the original source inventory; current comparison reports identify
native Lean production acceptance. This record grants no test success,
default harness adoption, Issue completion, proof discharge or release approval.
